articles.title: देश धान्ने क्षेत्रमै संकट, श्रमिक विदेश पठाउन बन्द !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । वैदेशिक रोजगारीबाट आउने रेमिट्यान्सले देशको अर्थतन्त्र धान्न सहयोग पु¥याइरहेका म्यानपावर व्यवसायीले सरकारविरुद्ध दबाब बढाएका छन् । १५ बुँदे माग अघि सार्दै नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले शुक्रवारदेखि वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द गर्ने घोषणा गरेको छ । व्यवसायीहरूले नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म कामदार नपठाउने अडान लिएका छन् ।

नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार क्षेत्रका नीतिगत समस्या समाधान नभएको भन्दै शुक्रवारदेखि श्रमिक विदेश पठाउने कार्य पूर्ण रूपमा स्थगित गरेको छ । काठमाडौँमा पत्रकार सम्मेलन गर्दै संघले रेमिट्यान्सले मुलुकको अर्थतन्त्रमा ठूलो योगदान पु¥याए पनि सरकारले समयानुकूल नीति सुधार नगर्दा व्यवसायी र श्रमिक दुवै प्रभावित भएको जनाएको छ ।

संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार ऐन–२०६४ लाई समयसापेक्ष संशोधन, पारदर्शी लागत निर्धारण, वैज्ञानिक सेवा शुल्क, श्रमिक लक्षित गन्तव्य मुलुकको हवाई भाडा घटाउने तथा कृत्रिम अभाव अन्त्य गर्न माग गरेको छ । युरोपका नयाँ श्रम बजार, दक्षिण कोरियाको ई–सेभेन भिसा, जापानको ईएसडी कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन, महिला घरेलु कामदारका लागि नयाँ गन्तव्य खुला गर्ने र विभिन्न मुलुकमा देखिएका प्रशासनिक तथा बिचौलिया समस्या कूटनीतिक पहलमार्फत समाधान गर्नुपर्ने माग पनि अघि सारिएको छ ।

संघले मागपत्र प्रमाणीकरण र श्रम स्वीकृतिलाई पूर्ण रूपमा स्वचालित बनाउन, ५ हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली श्रमिक रहेका मुलुकमा श्रम सहचारी तथा काउन्सिलर नियुक्त गर्न, व्यवसायीले राखेको धरौटीको ब्याज उपलब्ध गराउन र श्रमिकलाई बिना धितो सहुलियतपूर्ण कर्जा दिने व्यवस्था गर्न पनि सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ । अध्यक्ष खत्रीले विशेष परिस्थितिमा सरकारकै निर्णय कार्यान्वयन गर्दा व्यवसायीमाथि कारबाही गरिएको आरोप लगाउँदै अब नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म श्रमिक नपठाउने स्पष्ट चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

संघले आफ्ना सबै माग सम्बोधन नभएसम्म शून्य समय घोषणा गर्दै वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द रहने जनाएको छ । व्यवसायीहरूको यो निर्णयले वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान तयारी गरिरहेका हजारौं नेपाली श्रमिक प्रत्यक्ष प्रभावित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: सेती नदि थुनिएर ताल बन्यो, स्थानीय जाग्राम बस्न बाध्य
articles.summary:
कास्की । केहि दिन यताको निरन्तर वर्षाले पोखराको रामघाटमा सेती नदी थुनिएर विशाल ताल बनेको छ । जसका कारण नदिसँगै जोडिएका सुकुम्बासी बस्ती बाढीले बगाउने जोखिममा रहेका छन् ।

सेती नदीलाई लिएर पोखराको भौगोलिक बनावट अत्यन्त जोखिममा रहेको चर्चा गरिन्छ , तर सेतिले निम्त्याएको जोखिम न्यून गर्न भने कुनै निकायको ध्यान पुग्न सकेको छैन । झट्ट हेर्दा यो दृश्य कुनै तालको होला भन्ने लाग्न सक्छ, तर नझुक्किनुस् यो कुनै ताल भने होइन ।

केहीदिन यता निरन्तर परेको वर्षको कारण सेती नदीमा पानीको बहाव निकै उच्च छ । हो पोखरा रामघाटमा फराकिलो रहेको सेती नदीको निकास सानो हुँदा पानी जान नसकेर विशाल ताल नै बनेको छ । सेती नदी थुनिएर ताल बन्दा अहिलेसम्म क्षति त भएको छैन तर संभावित क्षतिको जोखिम भने निकै बढेको छ ।

दाह संस्कारका लागि बनाइएका घाटहरु पुरै जलमग्न बनेका छन् । सेती किनारसँगै दुई दर्जन बढी सुकुम्बासी बस्ती छ, बर्खा लागे पछि कतिबेला बाढीले बगाउने हो भनेर जाग्राम बस्नु पर्ने अवस्था छ । अहिले ३ वर्ष यताकै ठूलो र डरलाग्दो तरिकाले सेती बढेको स्थानीय बताउँछन् ।

सेती नदी पोखराको अधिकांस भागमा भूमिगत भएर बगेको छ । पोखराको बीच भाग अर्थात् रामघाटमा भने सेती सतहमा देखिन्छ । यस आसपासको क्षेत्र अत्यन्त जोखिममा रहेपनि सुकुम्बासीका नाममा बस्ती बस्ने क्रम भने नरोकिदो जोखिम झनै बढ्दैछ । पछिल्लो समय झनझन गहिरिदै गएको सेती खोंच र निरन्तरको बर्षाका कारण कतिबेला ठूलो दुर्घटना निम्तिने भन्ने इतिहासविद्को चिन्ता छ ।

पोखराको भू–बनोट र निरन्तर वर्षाले भासिन सक्ने सम्भाव्यताले पोखरालाई वर्षेनी जोखिम तर्फ धकेलेको भूगोलविद्को बुझाई छ । नदी थुनिएर आफ्नो गतिमा जान नपाउँदा निरन्तर जमिनलाई खियाउनाले जोखिम बढेको भूगोलविद् कृष्ण प्रसाद पौडेल बताउँछन् ।

पोखराको भू–बनोट, बेलाबेलामा भएका जमीन भासिने घटना र भूमिगतरूपमा बगेको सेतीका कारण पोखराको जोखिमबारे बेलाबेला चर्चा हुने गर्दछ, तर त्यो चर्चालाई दीर्घकालीन समाधानको बाटोतर्फ भने कुनै निकायले लैजान सकेका छैनन् ।

articles.title: स्तनपान प्रवद्र्धनमा जोड, दोलखामा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना
articles.summary:
दोलखा । जीवनको दिगो सुरुवातका लागि स्तनपान प्रभावकारी कार्यहरूको सुदृढीकरण“ भन्ने नारासहित दोलखाको भीमेश्वर नगरपालिका–५ स्थित माटी स्वास्थ्य चौकीमा विश्व स्तनपान सप्ताह–२०२६ मनाइएको छ । कार्यक्रममा गर्भवती तथा सुत्केरी आमाहरूलाई स्वास्थ्य सेवा, पोषण सामग्री वितरण तथा महिला स्वास्थ्य स्वयंसेविकालाई प्रोत्साहन गरिएको छ ।

विश्व स्तनपान सप्ताह–२०२६ को अवसरमा दोलखामा आयोजित कार्यक्रममा धुलिखेल अस्पताल दोलखाका विशेषज्ञ चिकित्सकहरूले गर्भवती महिलाको स्वास्थ्य परीक्षण, अल्ट्रासाउन्ड, स्वास्थ्य परामर्श तथा स्तनपान र शिशु पोषणबारे अभिमुखीकरण गरेका छन् ।

कार्यक्रममा गर्भवती तथा सुत्केरी आमालाई पोषण सामग्री, ब्ल्यांकेट तथा महिला स्वास्थ्य स्वयंसेविका र माटी स्वास्थ्य चौकीका स्वास्थ्यकर्मीलाई छाता वितरण गरिएको छ । ती सामग्री पूर्व स्वास्थ्य चौकी प्रमुख रामकृष्ण मास्केको पहलमा विभिन्न दाताबाट संकलन गरिएको हो ।

कार्यक्रममा जिल्लाको स्वास्थ्य अवस्था, शिशु स्वास्थ्यमा आमाको दूधको महत्व र स्तनपान प्रवद्र्धन अभियानबारे जानकारी गराइएको छ । समुदायस्तरमा यस्ता कार्यक्रमलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिइएको छ ।

भीमेश्वर नगरपालिकाले मातृ तथा शिशु स्वास्थ्यलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै स्वास्थ्य संस्थासँगको सहकार्यलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाउने जनाएको छ ।

नेपाल क्षयरोग निवारण संस्थाले समुदायमा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना अभिवृद्धिका कार्यक्रमलाई निरन्तरता दिइने जनाएको छ ।

कार्यक्रममा गर्भवती तथा सुत्केरी आमाहरूलाई स्वास्थ्य सेवा, पोषण सामग्री वितरण तथा स्वास्थ्य स्वयंसेविका र स्वास्थ्यकर्मीलाई सम्मान गर्दै स्तनपानको महत्व समुदायसम्म पु¥याउने प्रयास गरिएको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: भूपेन्द्रसहित बैंकका उच्च अधिकारीमाथि छानबिन शुरु
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । स्मार्ट टेलिकमको अर्बौं मूल्य बराबरको पूर्वाधार बिक्री प्रकरणले नेपालको दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्रमा ल्याएको तरंगको पराकम्प अझै कम भएको छैन । लाइसेन्स रद्द भएपछि राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनुपर्ने सम्पत्ति चार अर्ब ६० करोड रुपैयाँमा बिक्री भएको विषय अहिले अनुसन्धानको केन्द्रमा छ ।

सीआईबीले पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारीसहित बैंकका उच्च अधिकारीमाथि छानबिन अघि बढाएको छ । नेपालको दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्र एउटा प्रश्नले अझै तरंगित छ । राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनुपर्ने स्मार्ट टेलिकमको अर्बौं रुपैयाँ बराबरको सम्पत्ति कसरी निजी हातमा पुग्यो ? यसको जवाफ अझै मिल्न सकेको छैन । नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो अर्थात् सीआईबीले यही प्रकरणमा नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारीलाई पक्राउ गरी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाइरहेको छ ।

काठमाडौं जिल्ला अदालतले भण्डारीमाथि थप अनुसन्धानका लागि प्रहरीलाई ६ दिनको म्याद दिएको छ । उनीमाथि ठगी, आपराधिक विश्वासघात र संगठित अपराधसम्बन्धी कसुरमा अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ ।

स्मार्ट टेलिकमले २०७० सालमा आधारभूत टेलिफोन सेवा सञ्चालनको अनुमति पाएको थियो । तर कम्पनीले नवीकरण दस्तुर र रोयल्टीबापतको करिब ३० अर्ब रुपैयाँ सरकारलाई बुझाउन सकेन । त्यसपछि २०८० वैशाख ३ गते यसको लाइसेन्स स्वतः रद्द भयो ।

कानुनअनुसार लाइसेन्स रद्द भएको दूरसञ्चार कम्पनीको टावर, नेटवर्क, उपकरण र अन्य पूर्वाधार राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ । तर सीआईबीको आरोप छः राज्यको नाममा आइसकेको स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकले गैरकानुनी रूपमा लिलामी ग¥यो र त्यो सम्पत्ति एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडले खरिद ग¥यो । स्मार्टको लिलामी मूल्य थियो चार अर्ब ६० करोड रुपैयाँ ।

सीआईबीका अनुसार यो प्रक्रियामा तत्कालीन दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण अध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारीको भूमिका सबैभन्दा बढि शंकास्पद देखिएको छ । यही अनुसन्धानका क्रममा नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकका अध्यक्ष पृथ्वीबहादुर पाण्डेसहित ६ जना सञ्चालकको बैंक खाता रोक्का गरिएको छ । प्रहरीले उनीहरूविरुद्ध पक्राउ पुर्जीसमेत लिएको बताइएको छ ।

खाता रोक्का भएका व्यक्तिमा अध्यक्ष पाण्डेसँगै प्रणय राजभण्डारी, दीपांकर शाक्य, कविकुमार तिव्रेवाला, शालिकराम बेलवासे र शोभा श्रेष्ठ रहेका छन् ।

अर्का सञ्चालक मदनकुमार आचार्यले भने सीआईबीमा उपस्थित भएर बयान दिइसकेका कारण पक्राउ पुर्जीबाट बाहिर रहेको बुझिएको छ ।

फेरि एकपटक बिक्रि प्रक्रियाको कुरा गरौँ

स्मार्ट टेलिकमकोे सम्पत्ति बिक्री प्रक्रिया नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकले स्मार्ट टेलिकमले सम्पत्ति बिक्रिका लागि बोलपत्र आह्वान गरेसँगै अघि बढेको थियो । यसमा तीन कम्पनी सहभागी भए । ट्रान्सगेट टेकले ४४ करोड ५० लाख रुपैयाँ, प्रोफेसनल बिजनेस नेटवर्कले ४२ करोड ५० लाख रुपैयाँ र एनसेल आजियाटाले चार अर्ब ६० करोड रुपैयाँको प्रस्ताव पेस ग¥यो ।

बैंकले सबैभन्दा बढी रकम प्रस्ताव गर्ने एनसेलको बोलपत्र स्वीकार ग¥यो । तर यी तीन कम्पनीले राखेको खरिद मूल्य प्रस्ताव नै शंकास्पद देखिन्छ । सेटिङमै तीन कम्पनी एकै व्यक्तिबाट परिचालित देखिन्छ । दुई कम्पनीको प्रस्तावभन्दा एनसेल आजियाटाको प्रस्ताव आकाश जमिन फरक छ ।

यो किनबेचमा बैंकको दाबी छ, उसले ऋण असुलीका लागि बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थासम्बन्धी ऐनको व्यवस्थाअनुसार धितो बिक्री गरेको हो । तर जुन सम्पत्ति राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आइसकेको थियो, त्यसलाई बैंकले बिक्री गर्ने अधिकार कसरी पायो भन्ने सीआईबीको प्रश्न छ ।

यसअघि सीआईबीले स्मार्ट टेलिकमका सञ्चालक सर्वेश जोशी र नेपाल इन्भेष्टमेन्ट मेगा बैंकका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत ज्योति प्रकाश पाण्डेलाई पनि पक्राउ गरी अनुसन्धान गरेको थियो । सीआईबीले केही महिनादेखि यो प्रकरणमाथि अध्ययन अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

तत्कालिन मन्त्री शर्माको भूमिका !

भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष बन्नुअघि तत्कालिन सञ्चारमन्त्री रेखा शर्माका सल्लाहकार थिए । शर्माको जोडबलमा भण्डारीलाई प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्षमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल ‘प्रचण्ड’ नेतृत्वको सरकारले नियुक्त गरेको थियो । प्राधिकरण अध्यक्ष बन्नुअघि भण्डारी इन्टरग्रुप टेलिकम एसएल लिमिटेड र स्मार्ट मोबाइल बुरुन्डीको प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत भइसकेका व्यक्ति हुन् ।

उनले मरु डिजिटल वालेट चलाउने कम्पनी पेनेपमा अध्यक्षका रुपमा ५ वर्ष १० महिना काम गरेका थिए । कार्यकाल ७ महिना बाँकी छँदै प्राधिकरणका तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष पुरुषोत्तम खनालले तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्ड र तत्कालीन सञ्चारमन्त्री शर्माको दबाब खेप्न नसकेपछि २०८० पुस २४ गते राजीनामा दिएपछि भण्डारी दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्रको नियामक प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष नियुक्त भएका थिए ।

वर्तमान सरकारले सार्वजनिक पदाधिकारीसम्बन्धी विशेष व्यवस्थाअन्तर्गत भण्डारीलाई पदबाट बर्खास्त गरेको हो । आलोचकहरूले भण्डारीको कार्यकालमा दूरसञ्चार क्षेत्रका समस्या थप बढेको आरोप लगाएका छन् । स्मार्ट टेलिकमका टावर राख्न दिएका दुई सयभन्दा बढी घरधनीले समेत लामो समयदेखि भाडा नपाएको गुनासो गर्दै आएका छन् ।

सीआईबीको अनुसन्धानले राज्यको स्वामित्वमा आउनु पर्ने अर्बौ मूल्यको दूरसञ्चार पूर्वाधार कानूनी प्रक्रियाबाट बिक्रि भएको थियो कि मिलेमतोमा भन्ने प्रश्नको उत्तर खोजिरहेको छ । स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणको अन्तिम निष्कर्ष अनुसन्धान र अदालतको प्रक्रियाले तय गर्नेछ ।

articles.title: टुसा व्यापारमा कडाई, पोखरामा माग भन्दा कम आपूर्ति
articles.summary:
कास्की । साउन लागेसँगै पोखराको बजारमा पहाडी क्षेत्रमा पाइने औषधीय गुणयुक्त टुसाको कारोबार सुरु भएको छ । पोखरा घुम्न आउने पर्यटकका लागि टुसा लोकप्रिय कोसेली बन्दै गए पनि यस वर्ष उत्पादन र आपूर्ति घट्दा व्यापार पनि सुस्त बनेको छ ।

अन्नपूर्ण संरक्षण क्षेत्र आयोजनाले चोरी निकासी नियन्त्रण गरेसँगै बजारमा टुसाको उपलब्धता कम भएको जनाएको छ । पोखरा घुम्न आउने धेरैजसो आन्तरिक पर्यटक फर्किने बेला स्थानीय कोसेलीका रूपमा टुसा लैजान रुचाउँछन् ।

औषधीय गुणले भरिपूर्ण मानिने टुसाको तरकारी पछिल्ला वर्षहरूमा झन् लोकप्रिय बन्दै गएको छ । अधिकांश टुसा पाइने क्षेत्र अन्नपूर्ण संरक्षण क्षेत्र आयोजना (एक्याप) अन्तर्गत पर्छन् । संरक्षणसँगै स्थानीयको आयआर्जनलाई समेत ध्यानमा राख्दै एक्यापले हरेक वर्ष साउन महिनाभर सर्वसाधारणलाई टुसा संकलन गर्न अनुमति दिने गरेको छ ।

असारदेखि भदौसम्म टुसा पलाउने मुख्य याम हो । कास्कीका ल्वाङ, घलेल, भुर्जुङखोला, सिक्लेस, ताङतिङ, याङजाकोट, घान्द्रुक, लान्द्रुक, धम्पुस र लुम्लेलगायत उच्च पहाडी क्षेत्रबाट बजारमा टुसा ल्याइन्छ । मानव स्वास्थ्यका लागि उपयोगी भएकाले यसको महत्व हरेक वर्ष बढ्दै गएको एक्यापको भनाइ छ ।

साउन महिनामा धेरैले माछामासु कम खाने परम्परा र यही समयमा टुसाको उत्पादन बढी हुने भएकाले व्यापार पनि बढ्ने गरेको थियो । तर यस वर्ष भने बजारको अवस्था फरक देखिएको छ । व्यापारीका अनुसार उत्पादन कम भएकाले बजारमा टुसाको आपूर्ति घटेको छ ।

अहिले पोखरामा प्रतिमुठा ८० देखि १५० रुपैयाँसम्ममा बिक्री भइरहेको छ । राम्रो व्यापार भएका दिन एकै स्थानबाट दुई सय मुठासम्म बिक्री हुने गरे पनि अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा यसपालि कारोबार घटेको व्यवसायीको भनाइ छ ।

पछिल्ला वर्षहरूमा टुसाको चोरी निकासी बढेपछि एक्यापले व्यवस्थापन कडा बनाएको छ । बोलकबोल प्रक्रियामार्फत वैधानिक रूपमा संकलन र बिक्रीको व्यवस्था गरिएको छ ।

अघिल्ला वर्षमा करिब ९ लाख टुसा निकासा गरिएकोमा यस वर्ष ६ लाख मात्रै निकासा गरिएको र चोरी निकासी नियन्त्रण गरिएकाले पनि बजारमा टुसाको उपलब्धता कम भएको एक्यापले जनाएको छ ।

उच्च पहाडी क्षेत्रको प्राकृतिक उत्पादन टुसा जडीबुटी मात्र होइन, पोखराको पहिचान बनेको कोसेली पनि हो । तर उत्पादनमा कमी र अवैध निकासी नियन्त्रणको प्रभाव यस वर्ष बजारमा स्पष्ट देखिएको छ ।

संरक्षण र व्यवस्थित व्यवस्थापनसँगै उत्पादन बढाउन सकिए टुसाको व्यापारले स्थानीय अर्थतन्त्रलाई अझ बलियो बनाउने अपेक्षा समेत गरिएको छ ।

articles.title: महारथीको सम्मान लिन नेपाल आउँदै जनरल सेठ
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल–भारत सैनिक सम्बन्धको पुरानो परम्परालाई निरन्तरता दिन भारतीय स्थल सेनाप्रमुख जनरल धीरज सेठ साउन ३१ गते नेपाल भ्रमणमा आउँदैछन् । मानार्थ महारथीको सम्मान पाउने जनरल सेठको यो भ्रमणसँगै गोर्खा भर्ती, अग्निपथ योजना र सीमामा नेपाली नागरिकमाथि हुने व्यवहारका विषय पनि चर्चामा छन् ।

भारतीय स्थल सेनाका प्रमुख जनरल धीरज सेठ पाँच दिने औपचारिक भ्रमणका लागि साउन ३१ गते अर्थात् अगस्ट १६ मा नेपाल आउँदैछन् । नेपाली सेनाका प्रधानसेनापति अशोकराज सिग्देलको निमन्त्रणामा हुन लागेको यो भ्रमणलाई नेपाल–भारत सैनिक सम्बन्धको निरन्तरताका रूपमा हेरिएको छ ।

भ्रमणका क्रममा जनरल सेठलाई नेपाली सेनाको मानार्थ महारथी दर्जाको दज्र्यानी चिह्न प्रदान गरिने कार्यक्रम छ । सन् १९५० देखि नेपाल र भारतले एकअर्काका सेना प्रमुखलाई मानार्थ महारथीको सम्मान प्रदान गर्दै आएका छन् । यो परम्परालाई दुई देशबीचको विश्वास, मित्रता र सैनिक सहकार्यको एउटा विशिष्ट प्रतिक मानिएको छ ।

यसअघि २०८१ मंसिर २७ गते नेपाली सेनाका प्रधानसेनापति अशोकराज सिग्देललाई भारतको नयाँदिल्लीमा आयोजित विशेष समारोहमा भारतीय राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मुले भारतीय सेनाको मानार्थ महारथीको दज्र्यानी चिह्न प्रदान गरेकी थिइन् ।

नेपाल–भारत सैनिक सम्बन्ध !

नेपाल र भारतबीचको सैनिक सम्बन्ध शताब्दीयौँ पुरानो मानिन्छ । स्वतन्त्र भारत र नेपालबीच सन् १९५० को शान्ति तथा मैत्री सन्धिपछि दुई देशबीचको रक्षा सहकार्य अझ संस्थागत बनेको हो । दुवै देशका सेनाले संयुक्त सैन्य अभ्यास सूर्य किरण, विपद् व्यवस्थापन, सीमा सुरक्षासम्बन्धी समन्वय, तालिम आदान–प्रदान तथा उच्च तहका भ्रमणलाई निरन्तरता दिँदै आएका छन् ।

यस्तै नेपाली नागरिक भारतीय सेनामा भर्ती हुने व्यवस्था पनि दुई देशबीचको विशेष सम्बन्धको अर्को आधार हो ।

गोर्खा सैनिकका रूपमा नेपाली युवाले करिब दुई सय वर्षदेखि भारतीय सेनामा सेवा गर्दै आएका छन् । अहिले पनि हजारौँ नेपाली नागरिक भारतीय सेनाका विभिन्न गोर्खा रेजिमेन्टमा कार्यरत छन् भने ठूलो संख्यामा पूर्वगोर्खा सैनिकले पेन्सन र अन्य सुविधा प्राप्त गरिरहेका छन् ।

अग्निपथले रोकिएको भर्ति !

तर पछिल्ला वर्षमा भारतीय सेनाको अग्निपथ योजना लागू भएपछि नेपाली नागरिकको भर्ती प्रक्रिया प्रभावित भएको छ । नेपाल सरकारले अग्निपथ योजनाबारे औपचारिक धारणा नटुंग्याएको भन्दै नेपाली युवाको भारतीय सेनामा नयाँ भर्ती रोकिएको अवस्था छ ।

चार वर्षे कार्यकाल र त्यसपछि २५ प्रतिशतलाई मात्रै नियमित सेवामा राखिने अग्गिपथ अन्तर्गतको मापदण्डका कारण लामो समयदेखि कायम रहेको गोर्खा भर्ती रोकिएको हो । यो विषयमा दुवै देशबीच कूटनीतिक तहमा छलफल हुँदै आएको छ ।

सीमा दुखेको सम्बन्ध !

नेपाली सेना र भारतीय सेनाबीच मानार्थ महारथीको विशिष्ट परम्परा रहँदा रहँदै पनि सीमामा भारतीय सीमा सुरक्षा बल एसएसबीले नेपाली नागरिकमाथि गर्ने दुव्र्यवहारका घटना बेलाबेला सार्वजनिक हुँदै आएका छन् ।

एसएसबीले सीमा क्षेत्रमा कुटपिट, अनावश्यक नियन्त्रण, गोली चलाइएका घटना तथा नेपाली नागरिकमाथि भएको दुव्र्यवहारले नेपाली नागरिकले अक्सर भारतसँग चित्त दुखाउनु परेको छ । यस्ता घटनापछि नेपाली पक्षबाट कूटनीतिक विरोध भएपनि दीर्घकालीन समाधान भने हुन सकेको छैन ।

articles.title: वित्तीय क्षेत्रको निष्पक्षता नै अर्थतन्त्रको मेरुदण्डः एक्यान अध्यक्ष नेपाल
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल चार्टर्ड एकाउण्टेण्ट्स संघ (एक्यान) का अध्यक्ष अनुप नेपालले वित्तीय क्षेत्रको निष्पक्षता नै अर्थतन्त्रको मेरुदण्ड भएको बताएका छन् ।

नेपाल अडिटर्स एसोसिएसन (अडान) को वार्षिक साधारण सभालाई सम्बोधन गर्दै उनले मुलुकको अर्थतन्त्रमा पारदर्शिता र वित्तीय सुशासन कायम गर्न लेखापरीक्षण क्षेत्रको भूमिका महत्वपूर्ण हुने बताए । उनले राज्यको राजस्व सङ्कलनलाई पारदर्शी बनाउन र व्यावसायिक क्षेत्रमा विश्वास अभिवृद्धि गर्न लेखापरीक्षकहरूले गरेको योगदानको प्रशंसा गरे ।

एक्यान र अडान दुवै संस्थाको साझा लक्ष्य नेपाली लेखा व्यवसायलाई थप मर्यादित, पारदर्शी र उत्तरदायी बनाउनु रहेको भन्दै उनले पेसागत हकहित र नीतिगत सुधारका लागि सहकार्य आवश्यक रहेको बताए ।

उनले आजको समय प्रविधिमैत्री युग रहेको भन्दै यसमा पनि अडिटर्सहरुले आफूलाई प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय लेखापरीक्षण मापदण्ड र कर प्रणालीका नयाँ चुनौतीहरूको सामना गर्नका दक्षता अभिवृद्धि गर्नुपर्ने उनको सुझाव छ । पछिल्लो समयको एआई प्रविधिहरुबाट कोही पनि आतंकित हुनु नपर्ने भन्दै प्रविधिलाई केवल एउटा साधनका रूपमा लिन उनले आग्रह गरे ।

उनले क्याल्कुलेटरको आविष्कारको उदाहरण दिँदै क्याकुलेटर आज सामान्य र आवश्यक भएजस्तै एआई जस्ता प्रविधिहरु आगामी दशकमा उस्तै अत्यावश्यक बन्ने बताए ।

खासगरी उच्च व्यावसायिक नैतिकता, निष्पक्षता र इमानदारितालाई आत्मसाथ गरि समाज र राज्यको लेखापरीक्षण पेशाप्रतिको विश्वासलाई मजबुत बनाउनुपर्नेमा उनले जोड दिएका छन् ।

articles.title: गुप्तचर निकायमाथि चौतर्फि आलोचना, संयन्त्रमाथि गम्भिर प्रश्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सुनसरी घटनापछि राज्यको सुरक्षा संयन्त्रको मात्र होइन, राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागको भूमिका र औचित्यमाथि नयाँ बहस शुरु भएको छ । राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभाग प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय मातहत राख्ने कि गृहमन्त्रालय मातहत रहने भन्नेमा सांसदहरुबीच नै फरक फरक मत रहेका छन् । प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह पनि गुप्तचरी निकायको कामप्रति सन्तुष्ट हुन सकेका छैनन् ।

देशभित्र हुने भू–राजनीतिक चलखेल, वैदेशिक हस्तक्षेप, आन्तरिक अस्थिरता तथा आन्दोलनमा हुने घुसपैठको निगरानी गर्ने जिम्मेवारी बोकेको संस्था हो, राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभाग । तर प्रश्न उठ्छ के राअवि आफनो भूमिकामा प्रभावकारी छ ? पछिल्लो समय यसको प्रभावकारीता खस्कँदै गएको देखिन्छ । सरकारले पनि यसको भूमिका र महत्वप्रति आवश्यक चासो देखाउन छाडेको छ । संसदमा पनि अनुसन्धानको भूमिका माथि प्रश्नहरु उठाइएका छन् ।

नेपालमा किन गुप्तचर निकाय यति कमजोर बन्दै गएको छ ? दक्षिणी छिमेकी मुलुक भारतमा आन्तरिक सुरक्षाका लागि इन्टेलिजेन्स ब्यूरो आईबी र बाह्य रणनीतिक सूचनाका लागि रिसर्च एन्ड एनालाइसिस विंग ‘रअ’ छन् । यी सस्थाहरु कानुनी दायरा भित्र रहेर अत्यन्त शक्तिशाली रुपमा परिचालित छन । आबश्यक परेमा फोन ट्यापिङ समेत गर्न सक्ने अधिकार उनीहरुसँग छ । तर स्पष्ट कानुनी संरचना भित्र बसेर मात्र । भारतमा गुप्तचर प्रमुखहरू प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग प्रत्यक्ष संवाद गर्न सक्छन । तर नेपालमा गुप्तचर निकाय राअवि प्रधानमन्त्री मातहत रहेपनि प्रधानमन्त्रीसँग देशको सुरक्षा चुनौती बारे छलफल गर्न त परको कुरा सूचना संकलन गर्न समेत चुकेका छन् ।

अब लगौं केही घटना तर्फः साउन १० गते राति सुनसरीको कप्तानगन्जमा दुई समूहबीच विवाद सुरु हुँदा स्थानीय प्रहरी चौकीबाट खटिएको टोली नै आफैं आक्रमणमा पर्यो। स्थिति नियन्त्रण बाहिर गएपछि प्रहरी र सशस्त्रले दर्जनौँ राउन्ड हवाई फायर गर्नुप¥यो। तर प्रश्न यो उठ्छ— यति ठूलो साम्प्रदायिक तनावको पूर्वसूचना सुरक्षा निकाय र गुप्तचरले किन पाएन ?

गृहमन्त्रीले समेत घटनाअघि कुनै पनि निकायबाट पूर्वसूचना नआएको बताइसकेका छन्। सुनसरीमा अनुसन्धानका एसपी सरहका उपअनुसन्धान निर्देशक विमल घिमिरेको नेतृत्वमा टोली खटिएको थियो । प्रदेशमा डीआईजी सरहका अनुसन्धान निर्देशक इन्द्र लामा नेतृत्वको टोली खटिएको भए पनि उनीहरूले यसबारे सम्भावित द्वन्द्वको सुइँकोसमेत पाउन सकेन ।

सुनसरीमा स्थिति बिग्रिँदै गएपछि प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाहले नेपाल प्रहरीका प्रमुख दानबहादुर कार्की र सशस्त्र प्रहरी प्रमुख नारायणदत्त पौडेललाई प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयमा बोलाएर घटनाको विस्तृत ब्रिफिङ लिएका थिए । तर, यति ठुलो घटना हुँदा पनि प्रधानमन्त्रीले आफू मातहत नै रहेको गुप्तचर निकाय राअविका प्रमुख टेकेन्द्र कार्कीलाई भने बैठकमा बोलाएनन् ।

यस्तो छ अनुसन्धान विभागको संरचना र जिम्मेवारी

मुलुकभर राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागको संरचना छ । सिंहदरबार दक्षिण गेटसँगै विभागको मुख्यालय छ । विभागका २ हजार २६५ जना कर्मचारी र एजेन्टहरूलाई सूचना सङ्कलन गर्ने जिम्मेवारी दिइएको हुन्छ । जिल्ला इन्चार्ज र केन्द्रमा विभागीय प्रमुखले तोकेका एजेन्टहरूले पनि विभागलाई सूचना उपलब्ध गराउँछन् । मुख्य अनुसन्धान निर्देशकको नेतृत्वमा विभागमा दुई जना अतिरिक्त मुख्य अनुसन्धान निर्देशक हुन्छन् ।

९ जना अनुसन्धान निर्देशक छन् । अनुसन्धान निर्देशकहरू ७ वटा प्रदेश, उपत्यकामा र प्रशासन विभागमा छन् । सह–अनुसन्धान निर्देशक ११ जना छन् ।

काठमाडौँ, ललितपुर, त्रिभुवन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थल र हेटौंडास्थित इन्टेलिजेन्स शिक्षालयमा सहअनुसन्धान निर्देशकले कमाण्ड गर्छन् । उपअनुसन्धान निर्देशक ५३ जना र प्रमुख अनुसन्धान अधिकृत ९० जना छन् । अनुसन्धान अधिकृतहरू १६० जना छन् ।

विभागलाई सरकारले २ अर्बभन्दा बढी बजेट विनियोजन गर्दे आएकोमा यसपालि भने ५० प्रतिशत कटौती गरिएको छ । कार्यप्रकृतिअनुसार राअविले देशको राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामा असर पर्न सक्ने विषयमा सूचना संकलन गरेर घटना हुनुअगावै सरकारलाई जानकारी दिनुपर्ने हो । नेपाल प्रहरी र सशस्त्र प्रहरी घटना भइसकेपछि खटिने हुन्, अनुसन्धान जस्तो निकाय घटना हुनुअगावै परिचालित हुने हो । तर राअवि यही काममा पटक–पटक चुक्दै आएको छ, जसका कारण गुप्तचरका प्रतिवेदन र विश्लेषणलाई राजनीतिक नेतृत्वले प्राथमिकता दिन छाडेका छन ।

त्यसको असर गत बर्षको भदौ २३ मा भएको जेन–जी आन्दोलनमा देखिएको थियो,जति बेला राअविको एक साता अघिदेखिको प्रतिवेदन तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओलीले खोलेर हेरेकै थिएनन् । २०८१ चैत १५ गते तीनकुने क्षेत्रमा भएको दुर्गा प्रसाईं नेतृत्वको आन्दोलन तथा भदौ २३–२४ मा भएको जेन–जी आन्दोलनका क्रममा राज्य संयन्त्र पूर्वसूचना संकलनमा निकै कमजोर देखियो ।

आन्दोलनको स्वरूप, उद्देश्य तथा सहभागीबारे स्पष्ट जानकारी नहुँदा सुरक्षा निकायहरू आकस्मिक बल प्रयोग गर्नुपर्ने अवस्थामा पुगेका थिए ।

नेपाल दुई ठूला शक्ति भारत र चीनबीच रहेको संवेदनशील भूराजनीतिक अवस्थाको राष्ट्र हो । यस्तो अवस्थामा गुप्तचर संयन्त्र कमजोर हुँदा राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामा प्रत्यक्ष प्रभाव पर्न सक्ने चिन्ता व्यक्त गरिन्छ ।

खासमा प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले राअविलाई बलियो बनाउने भनेरै जेठ १ गते कार्यविभाजन नियमावली संशोधन गर्दै प्रधानमन्त्री तथा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को कार्यालय मातहत लगेका थिए । तर साउन १० मा भएको सुनसरी घटनामा राअविले न प्रधानमन्त्रीको विश्वास जित्न सक्यो, न त प्रभावकारी सूचना नै दिन सक्यो ।

अहिले त राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागलाई छाडेर नयाँ संरचना बनाउन पर्ने समेत आवज उठ्न थालेको छ ।

यस्तो छ गुप्तचर निकायको इतिहास ?

केन्द्रीय गुप्तचर विभागका रूपमा मंसिर २००८ मा स्थापना भएको राअवि विभिन्न समयमा नाम फेरिँदै अहिलेको अवस्थामा आइपुगेको हो । राअविकै सूचनाका आधारमा २०३२ साउन २७ गते नेपालस्थित एक दूतावासका अधिकारी मन्त्रिपरिषद्को माइन्युटसहित पक्राउ परेका थिए ।

यसमा तत्कालीन विद्युत् सहायकमन्त्री ध्यानबहादुर राईका निजी सचिव विजय चापागाईंसमेत मुछिएका थिए । २०५२ पछि माओवादी सशस्त्र संघर्ष उत्कर्षमा पुगेका बेला बेलायती खुफिया एजेन्सी एमआई–६ को सहयोगमा राअविले अपरेसन मुस्ताङ चलाएको थियो । कुनै बेला यो विभागलाई बाह्य जासुसी गर्ने जिम्मेवारीसमेत दिइएको थियो ।तर, २०४६ को परिवर्तनपछि यसलाई आन्तरिक गुप्तचरीको काममा मात्र सीमित गरियो ।

२०५० पछि यसलाई राजनीतिक दलले कार्यकर्ता भर्ती केन्द्र नै बनाएको देखिन्छ । संरचनागत रूपमा अहिले पनि राअवि पछाडि नै परेको देखिन्छ । यो विभागलाई नेपाली सेना, नेपाल प्रहरी र सशस्त्र प्रहरी बलपछि चौथो स्थानमा राखिएको छ। तर यो निकाय संवेदनशीलता र रणनीतिक महत्वका हिसाबले भने अग्रस्थानमा हुनुपर्ने हो । तर स्पष्ट संरचना र स्थायित्वको अभावका कारण यसको कार्यसम्पादन प्रभावित हुँदै आएको छ।

राअविको भूमिकामा राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप बढ्दै जाँदा संस्था अझ कमजोर बन्दै गएको विश्लेषण भइरहेको छ। प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय र गृह मन्त्रालयबीचको संरचनात्मक अस्पष्टताले पनि यसको कार्यक्षमतामा असर परेको देखिन्छ ।

articles.title: दैलेखको ग्यास परियोजना किन अलपत्र ?
articles.summary:
दैलेख । देशभर अहिले खाना पकाउने एलपी ग्यासको आपूर्ति सहज छैन । कतै उपभोक्ता सिलिन्डर बोकेर डिलरको ढोकामा लाइनमा छन्, कतै ग्यास पाउन दिनहुँ कुर्नुपर्ने अवस्था छ । ग्यास अभाव देखिँदा सर्वसाधारणको दैनिकी प्रभावित बनेको छ ।

एकातिर ग्यासको अभाव र आपूर्तिको चिन्ता छ, अर्कोतिर आफ्नै भूमिमा प्राकृतिक ग्यासको सम्भावना देखिएको परियोजना भने अहिले अलपत्र अवस्थामा छ ।

नेपालले हरेक वर्ष पेट्रोलियम पदार्थ र एलपी ग्यास आयातमा अर्बौं रुपैयाँ खर्च गर्दै आएको छ । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय बजारमा मूल्य वृद्धि वा आपूर्ति प्रभावित हुँदा त्यसको प्रत्यक्ष असर नेपाली उपभोक्ताले भोग्नुपर्छ । यता दैलेखको जलजले क्षेत्रमा प्राकृतिक ग्यासको सम्भावना देखिएको पेट्रोलियम अन्वेषण परियोजना भने पहिलो चरणको अध्ययनपछि अघि बढ्न सकेको छैन ।

नेपाल र चीन सरकारको सहकार्यमा सञ्चालित परियोजनाका लागि चीन सरकारले करिब २ अर्ब ४० करोड रुपैयाँ अनुदान दिएको थियो। चाइना जियोलोजिकल सर्भेले ४ हजार १३ मिटर गहिराइसम्म ड्रिलिङ गरी भूगर्भीय, भूभौतिक तथा भू–रासायनिक अध्ययन सम्पन्न गरेको थियो ।

अध्ययनले विशेषगरी मिथेन ग्यासको सम्भावना देखाएको छ । प्रतिवेदनले थप वेल टेस्टिङ गरी व्यावसायिक उत्पादनको सम्भाव्यता मूल्यांकन गर्न सिफारिस गरे पनि दोस्रो चरणको परीक्षण र लगानी योजना अघि बढ्न सकेको छैन । परियोजनाबाट रोजगारी र समृद्धिको आशामा स्थानीयले जग्गासमेत उपलब्ध गराएका थिए। तर योजना अलपत्र पर्ने हो कि भन्ने चिन्ता बढेको छ ।

रोजगारी र विकासको आशामा जग्गा दिएको स्थानीय बताउँछन् । तर यो परियोजना कागजमै सीमित हुने हो कि भन्ने चिन्ता उनीहरुमा देखिन्छ ।

देशको ऊर्जा भविष्यसँग जोडिएको यो परियोजनालाई स्थानीय, प्रदेश र संघीय सरकारले प्राथमिकताका साथ अघि बढाउनुपर्छ ।

दैलेखमा देखिएको सम्भावना प्रमाणित भई उत्पादन सुरु भए नेपाल ऊर्जा क्षेत्रमा आत्मनिर्भर बन्ने आधार तयार हुन सक्ने भैरवी गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्षको भनाइ छ ।

यो परियोजनामा पहिलो चरणमा प्रयोग भएका उपकरण लामो समयदेखि प्रयोगविहीन छन् । तिनको संरक्षण र आगामी योजनाबारे स्पष्ट जानकारी सार्वजनिक भएको छैन ।

परियोजनालाई अघि बढाउने विषय सम्बन्धित निकायको निर्णय र समन्वयमा निर्भर छ । अहिले नेपाल ग्यास र पेट्रोलियम आयातमै निर्भर छ । दैलेखको जलजले परियोजनालाई समयमै अघि बढाउन सके दीर्घकालमा ऊर्जा आयात घटाउने महत्वपूर्ण आधार बन्न सक्ने देखिन्छ ।

articles.title: पढ्दै गर्दा नै विश्वव्यापी कम्पनीसँग काम गर्दै इस्लिङ्टन कलेजका २९ विद्यार्थी
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालमै बसेर अध्ययनसँगै विश्वका विभिन्न कम्पनीका वास्तविक परियोजनामा काम गर्ने अवसर इस्लिङ्टन कलेजका २९ विद्यार्थीले पाएका छन् । कलेजले अघि सारेको ‘नेपालबाटै विश्वमा पहुँच’ भन्ने अवधारणालाई व्यवहारमै उतार्दै विद्यार्थीहरू अमेरिका, अस्ट्रेलिया र बेलायतका कम्पनीसँग जोडिएर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका परियोजनामा काम गरिरहेका हुन् ।

इस्लिङ्टन कलेजका लागि ‘नेपालबाटै विश्वमा पहुँच’ केवल प्रचारात्मक नारा नभई विद्यार्थीलाई देश नछोडीकनै विश्वस्तरमा प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्न सक्षम बनाउने शैक्षिक दृष्टिकोणका रूपमा अघि बढाइएको कलेजले जनाएको छ । यही उद्देश्यअनुसार कलेजले विभिन्न उद्योग तथा व्यावसायिक संस्थासँग सहकार्य गर्दै विद्यार्थीलाई पढाइसँगै व्यावहारिक अनुभव र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कार्य वातावरणमा काम गर्ने अवसर उपलब्ध गराउँदै आएको छ । कलेजका अनुसार विद्यार्थीले अध्ययनकै क्रममा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरको तालिम लिनुका साथै वास्तविक परियोजनामा सहभागी हुने अवसर पाउँछन् । यसका लागि डिग्री पूरा गर्नुपर्ने वा विदेश जानुपर्ने अवस्था छैन । काठमाडौंमै बसेर आफ्नो पढाइलाई निरन्तरता दिँदै उनीहरूले विश्वव्यापी टोलीसँग वास्तविक जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिरहेका छन् ।

अमेरिका, अस्ट्रेलिया र बेलायतका कम्पनीका लागि काम गरिरहेका २९ विद्यार्थीलाई कलेजले आफ्नो पहिलो कृत्रिम बौद्धिकता आधारित दक्ष विद्यार्थी समूहका रूपमा अघि सारेको छ । यी विद्यार्थीले आफ्नो मूल विषयसँगै आधुनिक कृत्रिम बौद्धिकता प्रविधिमा आधारित विश्वव्यापी कार्य वातावरणमा सोच्ने, निर्माण गर्ने र परिणाम दिन सक्ने सीप विकास गरेका छन् ।

कलेजले विद्यार्थीलाई वास्तविक परियोजना, उद्योगअनुकूल प्रयोगशाला, आधुनिक सुविधा र व्यावहारिक सिकाइमार्फत सुरुदेखि नै व्यावसायिक क्षेत्रका आवश्यकताअनुसार तयार पार्दै आएको जनाएको छ । त्यसकै परिणामस्वरूप विद्यार्थीहरू पढाइ पूरा हुनुअघि नै अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कम्पनीका वास्तविक काममा संलग्न हुन सफल भएको कलेजको दाबी छ ।

कलेजका अध्यक्ष सुलभ बुढाथोकीले विद्यार्थीले डिग्री पूरा गर्ने कि करियर सुरु गर्ने भन्ने दुईमध्ये एउटा रोज्नुपर्ने अवस्था नरहेको बताएका छन् । उनका अनुसार विद्यार्थीले अध्ययन र व्यावसायिक यात्रालाई एकसाथ अघि बढाइरहेका छन् ।

उनका अनुसार ‘नेपालबाटै विश्वमा पहुँच’ विद्यार्थीका लागि अवसर नेपालमै रहेको सन्देश दिने अभियानका रूपमा अघि बढाइएको हो । विद्यार्थीले अध्ययन पूरा गरेपछि मात्र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो व्यावसायिक यात्रा सुरु गर्नुपर्ने सोच परिवर्तन हुँदै गएको उनको भनाइ छ । इस्लिङ्टन कलेजका विद्यार्थीलाई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय परियोजनामा जोड्न विश्वव्यापी प्रविधि समूहसँग पनि सहकार्य गरिएको छ । यही सहकार्यअन्तर्गत २९ विद्यार्थी अमेरिका, अस्ट्रेलिया र बेलायतमा सञ्चालन भइरहेका विभिन्न परियोजनामा संलग्न छन् ।

यसैगरी, कृत्रिम बौद्धिकतामा आधारित बाह्य सेवा साझेदार संस्थाले पनि विद्यार्थीहरूको क्षमता र तयारीलाई सकारात्मक रूपमा मूल्यांकन गरेको छ । विश्वभरका प्रतिभाको खोजी, तालिम तथा प्रमाणीकरण गर्दै उनीहरूलाई व्यावसायिक टोलीसँग जोड्दै आएको उक्त संस्थाले सूचना प्रविधि विकास, डिजाइन, बजार व्यवस्थापन तथा सञ्चालनलगायतका क्षेत्रमा सहयोग गर्दै आएको बताइएको छ ।

उक्त संस्थाका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रशान्त केसीका अनुसार इस्लिङ्टन कलेजका विद्यार्थी प्राविधिक रूपमा दक्ष छन् । नयाँ कुरा सिक्न सहज हुनुका साथै उनीहरू सुरुदेखि नै कृत्रिम बौद्धिकतामा आधारित कार्य वातावरणमा काम गर्न तयार देखिएको उनको भनाइ छ । कलेजले विद्यार्थीहरूको यो उपलब्धिलाई केवल अभ्यासका लागि गरिएको परियोजनाका रूपमा नभई वास्तविक व्यावसायिक अनुभवका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेको छ । विद्यार्थीहरूले काठमाडौंमै बसेर आफ्नो नियमित अध्ययनलाई निरन्तरता दिँदै अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय टोलीमा जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिरहेका छन् । इस्लिङ्टन कलेजका अनुसार यसले नेपालमा अध्ययनरत विद्यार्थीका लागि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अवसर प्राप्त गर्न विदेश नै जानुपर्ने वा अध्ययन पूरा भएपछि मात्र व्यावसायिक यात्रा सुरु गर्नुपर्ने परम्परागत सोचलाई समेत चुनौती दिएको छ । सही तालिम, प्रविधि, वातावरण र अवसर उपलब्ध गराउन सके नेपाली विद्यार्थीले नेपालमै बसेर विश्व बजारमा प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्न सक्ने कलेजको विश्वास छ ।

कलेजको पहिलो कृत्रिम बौद्धिकता आधारित दक्ष विद्यार्थी समूहले पनि यही सम्भावनालाई व्यवहारमा प्रमाणित गरेको दाबी गरिएको छ । विद्यार्थीका लागि विश्वसँग काम गर्ने अवसर स्नातकपछि मात्र सुरु हुने नभई पढाइसँगै सुरु हुन सक्ने उदाहरणका रूपमा यसलाई लिइएको छ ।

यससँगै ‘नेपालबाटै विश्वमा पहुँच’ अब इस्लिङ्टन कलेजको अभियान वा नारामा मात्र सीमित नभई विद्यार्थीले नेपालमै बसेर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कम्पनीसँग काम गर्दै हासिल गरिरहेको वास्तविक अनुभव र उपलब्धिका रूपमा स्थापित हुँदै गएको कलेजले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: फोनिज उपत्यका समन्वय समितिद्वारा सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठको योगदानबारे चर्चा
articles.summary:
ललितपुर । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) उपत्यका समन्वय समितिले फोनिजको २७औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसरमा नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघका संस्थापक अध्यक्ष सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठको पत्रकारिता क्षेत्रप्रतिको योगदानबारे अन्तरक्रिया तथा छलफल कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरेको छ ।

ललितपुर उद्योग वाणिज्य संघ, मंगलबजार, पाटनमा आयोजित कार्यक्रममा वक्ताहरूले नेपाली पत्रकारिताको संस्थागत विकास, पत्रकारहरूको हकहितको संरक्षण तथा व्यावसायिक पत्रकारिताको आधार निर्माणमा सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठले पुर्‍याएको योगदान ऐतिहासिक र प्रेरणादायी रहेको बताए।

वक्ताहरूले पत्रकारितालाई लोकतान्त्रिक मूल्य–मान्यता, अभिव्यक्ति स्वतन्त्रता तथा उत्तरदायी सञ्चार अभ्याससँग जोड्न श्रेष्ठले खेलेको भूमिकाको स्मरण गर्दै नयाँ पुस्ताका पत्रकारले उहाँको योगदानबाट प्रेरणा लिनुपर्ने धारणा व्यक्त गरे।

श्रेष्ठले वि.सं. २००८ सालमा उहाँको नेतृत्वमा नेपाल पत्रकार संघ गठन भएको थियो, जसलाई नेपालमा पत्रकारहरूको पहिलो संगठित पेशागत संस्था मानिन्छ। पत्रकारहरूलाई एउटै छातामुनि संगठित गर्ने, उनीहरूको पेशागत हक–हितको आवाज उठाउने तथा पत्रकारितालाई संस्थागत स्वरूप दिन उहाँले महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निर्वाह गर्नुभएको विभिन्न ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज र अनुसन्धानहरूले उल्लेख छ।

यद्यपि, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघको संस्थापक अध्यक्षको विषय लामो समयदेखि विवादमा छ। एक पक्षले सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठलाई नै संस्थापक अध्यक्ष मान्नुपर्ने तर्क गर्दै आएको छ भने नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघले भने पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री कृष्णप्रसाद भट्टराईलाई संस्थापक अध्यक्षका रूपमा लिएका छन् ।

यही विषयलाई लिएर फोनिजलगायत विभिन्न संघसंस्थाहरूले ऐतिहासिक तथ्य र दस्तावेजका आधारमा सत्यनारायण बहादुर श्रेष्ठलाई आधिकारिक रूपमा संस्थापक अध्यक्ष घोषणा गर्न पटक–पटक माग गर्दै आएका छन्।

फोनिज उपत्यका समन्वय समितिले स्थापना दिवसलाई केवल औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा सीमित नराखी नेपाली पत्रकारिताका अग्रज व्यक्तित्वको योगदानबारे विमर्श गर्ने उद्देश्यले कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरिएको जनाएको छ।

articles.title: लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफको प्रथम क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल एमडी ३२५ अन्तर्गत डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफ, नेपाल (लायन वर्ष २०२६–२०२७) को प्रथम डिष्ट्रिक्ट क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा क्याबिनेट अफिसर्स इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम आइतवार सम्पन्न भएको छ । डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नर लायन अजय प्रसाद खनालको अध्यक्षतामा सम्पन्न उक्त क्याबिनेट मिटिङमा डिष्ट्रिक्ट भरिका लायन्स लिडरहरू, क्लब पदाधिकारी तथा सदस्यहरूको उत्साहजनक एवं उल्लेखनीय सहभागिता रहेको थियो । बैठकमा लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको मूल मन्त्र हामी सेवा गर्छौलाई आत्मसात गर्दै चालू लायन वर्षका रणनीतिक योजनाहरू, सेवा गतिविधि, नेतृत्व विकास तथा संगठन सुदृढीकरणका विषयमा गहन र रचनात्मक छलफल गरिएको थियो ।

विशेषगरी, लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको ग्लोबल कज अन्तर्गतका मुख्य क्षेत्रहरू मधुमेह, दृष्टि, भोक निवारण, पर्यावरण, बाल क्यान्सर, मानवीय कार्य, विपद् राहत र युवा जस्ता विश्वव्यापी प्राथमिकताका कार्यक्रमहरू लगायत डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नरका प्रायोरिटी प्रोजेक्ट तथा मानवीय सेवामूलक अभियानहरूलाई अझ प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढाउने, सदस्यता अभिवृद्धि गर्ने तथा क्लबहरूको सक्रियता र क्षमता विकास बढाउने विषयमा महत्वपूर्ण निर्णयहरू समेत गरिएको छ ।

सोही अवसरमा उपस्थित विशिष्ट नेतृत्वको समुपस्थितिमा नयाँ क्याबिनेट टिमको औपचारिक इन्स्टलेसन (शपथ ग्रहण तथा पदस्थापना) सम्पन्न गरिएको थियो । नवगठित क्याबिनेट टिमले जिम्मेवारी ग्रहण गर्दै आगामी कार्यकालमा समाजमा प्रभावकारी सेवा तथा सबल नेतृत्व प्रदान गर्ने सामूहिक प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेका छन् ।

यस कार्यक्रमलाई भक्तपुर दिबेश्वरी लायन्स क्लबले आतिथ्यता तथा व्यवस्थापकीय सहयोग प्रदान गरेको थियो । उक्त भव्य कार्यक्रमले सम्पूर्ण लायन्स सदस्यहरूमा सेवाभाव, आपसी एकता र समर्पणको भावना अभिवृद्धि गर्दै समाजसेवामा अझ सक्रिय, उर्जावान र प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढ्न ठूलो प्रेरणा दिएको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: Widespread server crashes point to Nepal’s digital state failure
articles.summary:
Nepal’s ambitious push to build a paperless, digitally empowered state is running into a basic problem: the systems meant to deliver public services are increasingly unable to keep up with demand.

From government offices inside Singha Durbar to ward offices in the high mountains, digital platforms are being hit by server crashes, operational bottlenecks and prolonged service outages. What were intended to make public services faster and more accessible have, in many cases, become new points of delay and disruption.

The failures are no longer isolated incidents. They have become a recurring feature of public administration.

Critical systems, including the central National Identity Card (NID) verification network, land revenue and property registration databases, transport management portals, immigration systems at international gateways and national tax platforms, have all experienced serious disruptions.

Officials and technology experts point to a combination of obsolete hardware, shortsighted technological planning, flawed public procurement, heavy dependence on foreign vendors and a shortage of specialised technical personnel in the civil service.

Over the past decade, government agencies have digitised large parts of their operations, introducing dozens of software applications and online portals. These include the Line Ministry Budget Information System (LMBIS), managed by the Ministry of Finance; the Subnational Treasury Regulatory Application (Sutra), used by local governments for budget planning and financial reporting; the Integrated Tax Management System (ITMS), deployed across the Inland Revenue Department and regional tax offices; and citizen-facing systems such as the Nagarik App and the National ID Information System.

But the proliferation of digital platforms has not been matched by the infrastructure, interoperability and technical capacity needed to sustain them. In several documented cases, system failures have shut down entire public departments for weeks or even months, disrupting commerce, legal transactions and routine civic activities.

NID becomes a national bottleneck

At the centre of the latest disruption is a growing crisis in the central National Identity Card database operated by the Department of National ID and Civil Registration.

Designed as Nepal’s single source for biometric and demographic verification, the NID system has become a potential single point of failure as more services make NID verification mandatory. Banks, telecommunications companies, the Department of Transport Management and the Department of Passports send automated verification requests to the central database rather than storing raw biometric data locally.

The rapid expansion of connected agencies has, however, overwhelmed the system. Department officials say its primary storage and biometric-matching engine, the Multi-Biometric Server Infrastructure (MSI), has reached total saturation.

Designed in 2018 to handle up to 6,000 real-time verification requests per hour, the system now struggles to process just 600 to 700 requests a day, creating queues at public offices nationwide.

Information technology experts say the breakdown was predictable because capacity was not expanded alongside demand.

Vivek Rana, a senior information systems architect, said the government connected high-traffic systems to the central server without adequate investment in processing, storage and hardware.

“Over the past few years, high-traffic public and private sector systems were aggressively tethered to the central NID server without any corresponding investment in expanding the system’s processing bandwidth, data storage capacity, or server hardware,” Rana said. “When thousands of simultaneous verification requests hit the central server during peak business hours, the infrastructure simply collapses under the load, causing severe verification delays or complete system lockouts.”

Rana said the problem also reflects architectural incompatibility. Older government platforms often use XML-based Application Programming Interface (API)s while newer applications use RESTful models. Connecting them requires middleware to translate between the systems, which can slow processing and introduce instability when query volumes rise.

The result is an architecture where adding more services to a central system can increase, rather than reduce, the risk of failure.

Nationwide administrative paralysis

The crisis extends beyond identity services. Repeated failures of government software have disrupted critical sectors and, at times, brought essential services to a standstill.

At Tribhuvan International Airport, repeated crashes of immigration servers have delayed international flights, stranded passengers and forced officers to use paper records, creating security concerns.

The Department of Land Management and Archive faced a similar crisis last month when its Public Access Model (PAM) software failed, bringing down servers at Land Revenue Offices in all 77 districts. Land transfers, property registrations, mortgage processing and bank loans backed by property collateral were halted for weeks, freezing millions of rupees in transactions.

Transport services have also been affected. A three-week outage of the Department of Transport Management’s Electronic Driving Licence (EDL) and Vehicle Registration System (VRS) prevented citizens from applying for or renewing licences, adding vehicle categories, paying road taxes and scheduling driving examinations. The resulting backlog remains unresolved.

Anatomy of systemic failure

IT and e-governance experts attribute the recurring failures to flawed planning, weak system design and an outdated procurement model that treats complex software projects like traditional construction contracts.

Monohar Kumar Bhattarai, an e-governance specialist and former government IT policy adviser, said agencies focus on procurement rather than the full operational lifecycle of technology.

“Government agencies spend months navigating complex tender processes, but pay virtually no attention to how a system will perform over its entire operational lifecycle,” Bhattarai said. “Contracts are regularly awarded without establishing binding service-level agreements (SLAs), operational uptime guarantees, or clear maintenance frameworks. When you ignore the comprehensive lifecycle of information technology, catastrophic failures become guaranteed.”

Rana said fundamental design requirements, including expected users, peak traffic, storage and security needs, are often overlooked. Digital projects are frequently launched without feasibility studies or capacity forecasts.

Government IT personnel in Singha Durbar privately acknowledge that some projects are initiated to demonstrate visible progress, while long-term budgets for maintenance, upgrades and patching are neglected.

“Several years ago, while stationed in the remote mountain district of Humla, I oversaw the procurement and installation of approximately 80 million rupees worth of specialised server hardware across 14 regional land revenue offices,” a senior government IT officer said, speaking anonymously.

“However, over the next eight to ten years, not a single rupee was allocated to upgrade, service, or maintain those machines. Today, that expensive hardware is entirely obsolete and non-functional.”

The officer said officials are also reluctant to seek upgrade funds because of possible administrative scrutiny or corruption investigations.

“Technical personnel often struggle to convince non-technical ministry secretaries of the invisible necessity of software maintenance, leading the government to consistently starve systems of operational funding,” the officer said.

The foreign vendor lock-in trap

Flawed planning is compounded by heavy dependence on foreign technology firms and private contractors for critical government systems.

Nepal’s National Identity Card system, for example, was built using proprietary technology supplied by French multinational Idemia, formerly Oberthur Technologies and now IN Group. Because the platform is closed-source, the government does not own the underlying source code or database design.

Department engineers are therefore unable to independently modify the software, expand database fields or resolve internal bugs. Even minor technical problems can require assistance from Idemia’s technical team in France. Officials privately complain that vendors treat Nepal as a low-priority client, with delays in deploying technical fixes leaving public services disrupted for days.

The vulnerability extends beyond NID. A Ministry of Finance investigation report on Systemic Improvements in Information Technology for Public Financial Management found that dozens of critical government platforms remain heavily dependent on external contractors.

The report said ministries acquired proprietary software over two decades through foreign aid programmes funded by institutions including the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank. Systems deployed across the Ministry of Finance, Financial Comptroller General Office, Department of Customs and Department of National ID were often acquired without source codes or technical documentation.

Clause 3.3 of the report states: “Ministry departments and subordinate agencies display an excessive dependency on external service providers for the operation, maintenance, development, and upgrading of their core IT systems. Critical technical operations—including system configuration, database troubleshooting, security patching, and structural upgrades—are handled almost exclusively by external contractors.”

Paying for hardware, neglecting software

The problem is worsened by the government’s reluctance to purchase formal Software Support Contracts (SSC) after acquiring software. While offices routinely sign Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) for physical equipment, continuing software support is often avoided because of annual fees.

“When a government department refuses to purchase a software support contract, internal staff are left completely helpless when the software encounters a bug or database corruption,” IT expert Rana said. “Civil servants are forced to rely on trial-and-error troubleshooting, or informally plead with private technicians and acquaintances for off-the-record advice to keep national databases running.”

International vendors typically charge annual support fees of 15 to 20 percent of the original software cost. For specialised systems such as the Debt Management and Financial Analysis System (DMFAS), annual support can cost $150,000 to $350,000, making approval of recurring payments difficult under current budget rules.

Without support, systems can miss security patches, operating-system updates, database backups and bug fixes. SSL certificates, software licences, firewall subscriptions and antivirus services can also expire.

The Department of Printing’s web portal, which archives national gazettes, parliamentary acts and government ordinances, illustrates the problem. Its expired SSL certificate has caused browsers to flag the official legal repository as an “Unsecure Site” and blocked some users on secure networks from accessing public legislation.

Statutory hurdles and human-resource shortages

Government IT officials have long argued that the Public Procurement Act is poorly suited to rapidly changing technology. Although recent rules allow offices, in principle, to allocate up to 20 percent of a software system’s initial cost for annual maintenance, service contracts can still require lengthy 21-day or 30-day bidding processes. A critical system can therefore remain paralysed while procurement is completed.

The rules also provide limited mechanisms for assessing specialised software or calculating full lifecycle costs. Procurement committees often select the lowest bidder under the L1 model, leaving agencies with cheap, insecure or poorly developed systems.

The regulatory weakness is compounded by a shortage of skilled IT professionals.

Govinda Ram Paneru, an IT under-secretary at the Ministry of Finance, said the government lacks the expertise needed to manage complex digital infrastructure.

“Managing an enterprise-grade digital infrastructure is like running a major tertiary hospital; it requires highly specialised medical professionals across different disciplines,” Paneru said. “Similarly, a robust digital government requires specialised domain experts, system architects, senior programmers, database administrators, and cybersecurity specialists. Nepal’s civil service suffers from a structural absence of such technical expertise.”

Government IT units are often severely understaffed. The Department of Transport Management, for example, manages driving licences, vehicle registrations and road-tax records for millions of vehicles but has only three technical employees.

Frequent transfers also weaken institutional memory, forcing incoming officers to spend months understanding legacy systems before being able to address problems.

“The state harbours grand ambitions of delivering seamless digital governance, but makes zero investment in cultivating internal technical capacity,” Paneru said. “The government attempts to run massive national databases relying on a single computer engineer.”

Much of the underlying infrastructure is also obsolete. Most government data-centre servers and operating systems are seven to eight years old and have reached “End-of-Life” or “End-of-Support” status. Manufacturers have discontinued support and replacement parts, yet agencies continue operating the equipment because replacing it can trigger bureaucratic scrutiny.

The imperative for structural reform

Experts and senior officials say superficial fixes cannot address the structural weaknesses undermining Digital Nepal.

The first priority should be moving away from fragmented servers housed in individual ministries towards a unified national cloud architecture. Modern cloud systems can scale resources with demand, balance workloads and maintain secondary-server redundancies, reducing the risk that traffic spikes will bring down critical services.

The government should also reduce dependence on proprietary foreign technology by adopting open-standard frameworks. While complex core engines may still need to come from global vendors, secondary modules, citizen interfaces and API connectors could be developed locally using open architecture, giving Nepali engineers greater control over system integration and modification.

Experts say the government must reform the Public Procurement Act to reflect the software lifecycle, establish competitive salaries to attract and retain skilled technology professionals, and require regular technical audits and performance evaluations of active government databases.

articles.title: After Gen Z crackdown failure, Nepal Police to get new riot control gear
articles.summary:
The government has prioritised the procurement of non-lethal crowd control equipment following widespread criticism over the deaths of four people in recent security firings during communal tensions in the Tarai-Madhesh region.

Alongside equipment purchase, the Ministry of Home Affairs has initiated preparations to amend relevant security legislation and introduce advanced technologies, including drones capable of firing tear gas and broadcasting public announcements.

Speaking to Kantipur, Home Minister Sudan Gurung said a lack of funds had delayed non-lethal equipment purchases. However, with the new budget cycle now active, formal procurement procedures are underway.

“Operating under the old budget limited our ability to make new purchases,” said Gurung. “Now, as the procurement process starts, we aim for all types of non-lethal weapons necessary for effective crowd management.”

Gurung explained that the new strategy centres on using drones for surveillance, public announcements, and tear gas deployment. “Drones will enhance crowd management through real-time monitoring from a central command and by strengthening physical barricades,” said Gurung. “Our primary focus is on protecting vital infrastructure without causing human casualties.”

The push for crowd control infrastructure upgrades hinges on past security failures. During the Gen Z demonstrations on September 8 last year, protesters easily breached police barricades outside the parliament building in New Baneshwar. The lapse led security personnel to open fire indiscriminately.

Security officials cited the Essential Goods Protection Act, which authorises the Special Task Force to use lethal force if crucial infrastructure faces imminent threat.

To prevent similar escalations, the home ministry is preparing comprehensive amendments to both the Essential Goods Protection Act 1955 and the Local Administration Act 1971.

“We are drafting amendments after extensive consultations,” said Gurung. “Rather than making piecemeal changes repeatedly, we intend to introduce clear, durable legal revisions after thorough discussion.”

The minister noted that many security personnel still operate under an outdated mindset that defaults to live ammunition when tension escalates. “We want to transform that mindset and establish an administrative system that prioritises non-lethal alternatives,’ he said.

The need for legal and logistical reform was previously highlighted by the judicial commission led by former judge Gauri Bahadur Karki, which investigated the violence during the Gen Z protests last year. The Karki Commission recommended amending the Local Administration Act 1971 to clearly define parameters governing when security forces may open fire during curfews.

The commission's report also underscored a chronic shortage of basic non-lethal protective equipment, including body armour, shields, and tear gas.

Past procurement attempts often stalled due to controversy and procedural cancellations. Former inspector general of police Deepak Thapa recalled that a proposal to acquire Rs760 million worth of non-lethal riot control equipment—including tear gas, shotguns, rubber bullets, and riot gear—was cancelled at the last moment.

“The Ministry of Finance had assured the required funding, and the tender process was well advanced,” said Thapa. “However, disputes arose, forcing us to cancel the deal even after opening the letter of credit.”

Data from the Police Headquarters, Naxal shows that Nepal Police has not purchased significant quantities of tear gas since the 2020-21 fiscal year. Police bought 4,000 tear gas canisters annually in 2019-20 and 2020-21, following purchases of 6,000 canisters in 2018-19 and 10,000 canisters in 2017-18.

The prolonged procurement freeze forced officers to rely on expired tear gas during major demonstrations, drawing sharp public criticism.

Minister Gurung, however, claimed that expired tear gas had not been deployed under his leadership.

“Our first priority is de-escalating tension through dialogue,” said Gurung. “Even when force becomes unavoidable, using expired tear gas is strictly prohibited, and security forces are not using it.”

Senior police officials argue that reliance on live ammunition often stems from a lack of alternatives and insufficient training.

“If security personnel had adequate non-lethal weapons, they would not resort directly to live bullets,” said a deputy inspector general, speaking on condition of anonymity. “Regular practical training is equally lacking. When officers receive only five or six rounds of practice during training, asking them to shoot below the knee in a live conflict rarely yields precise results. The state must prioritise continuous training and avoid cancelling equipment tenders whenever controversy arises.”

To avoid commercial disputes, former IG Thapa suggested procuring equipment through government-to-government (G2G) agreements. “Unhealthy competition among private contractors and commission bargaining are the main drivers of tender disputes,” said Thapa. “The G2G procurement would eliminate those issues entirely.”

In addition to riot control, the home ministry is focusing on digital security and internal administrative tracking.

“We are currently unprepared for digital threats or cyberattacks targeting government infrastructure,” said Gurung. “We are digitising our internal systems so that every directive issued to staff can be tracked in real time from my desk to verify implementation.”

Former deputy inspector general Bhim Prasad Dhakal welcomed the focus on non-lethal technology, recommending digital upgrades along border corridors. “Installing AI-enabled gates, CCTV cameras, and X-ray scanners at border crossings will help police monitor illegal activities and improve overall crime prevention,” said Dhakal.

articles.title: Prime Minister Shah to meet Indian, Chinese envoys on Monday, US Chargé d’Affaires next day
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah is set to begin one-on-one meetings with Kathmandu-based key diplomatic stakeholders on Monday, breaking his self-imposed rule of avoiding individual engagements with foreign ambassadors.

Shah will meet Indian Ambassador Naveen Srivastava and Chinese Ambassador Zhang Maoming separately on Monday, before holding a similar meeting with the US Embassy’s Chargé d’Affaires Scott Urbom on Tuesday. Even as Shah had planned to meet them two weeks back the plan was deferred following the communal violence in Sunsari and other districts.

The decision to meet the ambassadors of Nepal’s two immediate neighbours on the same day appears intended to underscore their equal importance to Nepal, although the scheduling retains the government’s stated foreign policy priority of engaging India first, followed by China.

“The Indian ambassador is told to come first followed by the Chinese ambassador. So both ambassadors are meeting the prime minister on the same day, but the earlier and later timings also show the foreign policy priority of the government,” a senior Foreign Ministry official told the Post. “The next day, the prime minister will meet the acting US ambassador, who is Nepal’s other important and friendly development partner with a long history.”

Srivastava will call on Shah at the Prime Minister’s Office in the first half of Monday, while Zhang will meet him in the second half of the day. The Foreign Ministry has communicated the appointments to the respective embassies, according to a prime ministerial adviser.

“It is only natural to begin with the ambassadors of our two neighbours, India and China, given Nepal’s foreign policy priorities,” said an aide to the prime minister.

The meetings will be the first one-on-one courtesy calls between Shah and Kathmandu-based ambassadors since he became prime minister on March 27. The agenda is expected to be largely introductory, with the ambassadors briefing Shah on the state of bilateral relations and conveying any messages from their respective governments.

It has yet to be decided which officials will attend the meetings. Foreign Ministry officials, most likely the respective division heads, are expected to accompany the ambassadors, along with officials from the Prime Minister’s Office.

The only exception to Shah’s earlier policy of avoiding individual meetings with foreign representatives was his meeting with Asian Development Bank President Masato Kanda, who visited Nepal for three days beginning July 6.

Shah had initially adopted a policy of avoiding one-on-one meetings not only with ambassadors but also with visiting senior foreign officials. He declined requests from the US Embassy in Kathmandu for meetings with US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Samir Paul Kapur and President Donald Trump’s special envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor.

US Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy Sarah B. Rogers also did not receive an audience with Shah during her visit to Nepal.

Instead, Shah held joint meetings with Kathmandu-based ambassadors on April 9 and May 26. The move was widely welcomed by Nepali diplomats, foreign policy experts and observers, who viewed the group meetings as a more transparent and equitable approach to diplomatic engagement.

The policy, however, was increasingly seen as difficult to sustain as Shah began broadening his engagement with domestic stakeholders.

After his government completed 100 days in office, political adviser Asim Shah and other advisers recommended that the prime minister begin meeting domestic stakeholders, including businesspeople, media representatives and contractors as well as Kathmandu-based ambassadors, according to a prime ministerial aide.

The plan for individual meetings with ambassadors was subsequently put on hold following sudden protests and violent demonstrations in the Tarai-Madhesh region.

In recent weeks, however, Shah has increasingly moved away from his earlier reluctance to meet stakeholders individually. He has been holding consultations with Madhesh-based political parties and lawmakers and meeting business representatives, including traders, contractors, industrialists and exporters.

His decision to begin one-on-one diplomatic meetings is part of that broader shift in his style of engagement, according to the aide.

articles.title: As Nepali women’s choices expand, marriage becomes an option
articles.summary:
At 29, Reema Bhusal (name changed) finds herself answering a question she never imagined would become hers: What if she never married?

Marriage is considered a key milestone for women, something that makes or breaks a woman’s life. In Nepal, strong social value is attached to ramro keta sanga bihe (marriage to a good man). Without it, society often questions a woman’s status, her worth. Marriage is treated as the ultimate marker of stability, respectability and adulthood.

Yet beneath this tradition, a quiet rethinking is taking place. More women are questioning whether marriage is a necessity or simply a social expectation. While the number of women choosing to remain unmarried is still small, rising education, employment and financial independence are allowing some women to imagine lives outside traditional marital roles.

According to the 2021 National Population and Housing Census, the share of Nepali women who have never married beyond age 35 by choice has risen from virtually none in 1961 to 0.7 percent in 2021. The number is small, but the trend signals a shift: For many women, marriage is no longer a compulsion but a choice.

A similar shift is taking place in South Korea, where a growing number of women describe themselves as bihon—a term that means “willfully unmarried” or “no marriage”. The movement rejects the expectation that women should marry, have children and assume the load of unpaid domestic work.

For Bhusal, marriage was never presented as a choice growing up. Instead, she accepted it as something that happened to everyone. “It felt as unquestionable as the sun rising in the east,” she says.

“It wasn't a question of whether I wanted it, but rather how I would go about it.” She believed that if marriage was inevitable, she should at least find someone she could get along with.

A turning point came when a relationship she expected could end up in marriage failed. The breakup led her to question why she was pursuing an institution she had never fully believed in.

It also made her question the expectations placed on wives and daughters-in-law and come to see marriage as an unequal institution where women were often expected to sacrifice more than men. Reports of violence against women and the inequalities embedded in everyday customs only deepened those doubts.

“For me, financial independence and emotional independence eventually made it possible to imagine a different future,” she says.

Bhusal also rejects the common argument that marriage and parenthood are necessary to avoid loneliness in old age.

“The idea that you should marry and have children so that they can take care of you later feels deeply self-serving to me,” she says. “If that is the primary motivation for bringing life into the world, then I don't think it's a fair or honest one.”

Today, Bhusal says she is “genuinely comfortable with the possibility” that she may never marry. Although she describes herself as “a pendulum” — pulled by family expectations and social pressure, she no longer sees remaining single as a failure, but as a legitimate and peaceful way of living.

Unlike Bhusal, whose views evolved over time, 34-year-old feminist writer Nirvana Bhandary says her decision not to marry is a “conscious rejection” of the institution of marriage itself.

Bhandary credits financial independence and education with making that choice possible. “It’s only when you have the space to ask if marriage is actually necessary, then only you can reject it," she says, arguing that opting out of marriage remains a privilege unavailable to many women who are financially dependent or have never been exposed to alternative ways of thinking.

Over the years, after watching both arranged and love marriages around her, Bhandary came to see marriage as a patriarchal institution whose historical roots cannot be separated from unequal gender roles. “I don't see it making me happier or improving my life in any meaningful way,” she says.

While she acknowledges that many women reject the unequal expectations placed on wives and daughters-in-law, her disagreement goes further. “For many of us, it's about fundamentally disagreeing with the institution of marriage itself.”

Yet rejecting marriage does not mean rejecting companionship.

Bhandary says emotional and sexual intimacy need not be confined to marriage.

“Marriage is just an institution,”she says. “Love and intimacy are available in abundance without it as well.”

Rather than remaining single for life, Bhandary envisions a long-term partner with whom she can build a relationship on her own terms. "I definitely would like to have a life partner," she says. "But we can design a model of our relationship that suits our needs. It doesn't have to follow socially constructed definitions or boundaries of what is considered an acceptable relationship."

For Bhandary, the decision is not about rejecting love, but rejecting the belief that marriage is the only legitimate way to experience it.

Unlike Bhusal and Bhandary, 39 year old writer, Nirupa Prasun, says she never imagined marriage as part of her life. From childhood, she says, she viewed it as a restriction rather than a milestone.

“I always felt that marriage is a kind of restriction. I never wanted to be bound by it. I always wanted to live freely, like a bird,”she says.

After witnessing relationships break down around her, her conviction of not wanting to become someone's wife strengthened.

Yet, for Prasun, rejecting marriage has not meant rejecting motherhood.

As she entered her thirties, Prasun found herself longing for a child. Financially independent, she believes she has the means to raise one on her own.

“I’m financially independent. I have the means to raise a child,” she says.

But what holds her back is not the practical challenge of single parenthood; it is the fear of hurting her family. She fears that becoming a mother outside marriage would bring stigma not only upon herself but also upon her parents and brother’s family.

She says she has repeatedly gathered the courage to discuss the idea but has never been able to do so. “I cannot bear the thought of causing my parents pain by becoming a mother outside marriage,” she says, describing her desire for motherhood and loyalty to her family as a moral dilemma she has yet to resolve.

Although her parents have never pressured her to marry and have respected her decision, her mother still worries about her daughter's future and hopes she will one day change her mind.

"After I die, Yama [the god of death] will ask if I married off all my children,” her mother often tells her. “If I haven't done it for one daughter, he will send me to hell.”

Assistant Professor Dr Neeti Aryal Khanal of Tribhuvan University, says the growing number of women consciously choosing not to marry should be understood as part of broader social transformation rather than simply as resistance to marriage.

“We cannot simply say that it is resistance to marriage,” she says. “Human beings have an essential need for emotional connection. We all want someone to care for us and someone we can care for.”

According to Khanal, women choosing to remain unmarried is not a new phenomenon. What has changed, she says, is its visibility and the growing number of women able to make that choice.

Historically, marriage provided women with financial security and social acceptance at a time when gender roles confined them largely to homemaking and caregiving. Education, employment and financial independence have since expanded women’s choices, allowing many to decide not only whom to marry, but whether to marry at all.

At the same time, Khanal says, expectations within marriage have not changed as quickly as women’s lives outside it. “While the ratio of women participating in higher education and paid work has plummeted, they are still often expected to shoulder most domestic and caregiving responsibilities after marriage.”

For some, she says, that imbalance makes marriage appear as a loss of autonomy rather than a partnership.

Khanal cautions, however, against generalising all unmarried women.

Some consciously reject marriage as an institution, while others remain single because they do not fit society’s expectations of the “ideal wife” or “ideal daughter-in-law.”

She also notes that marriage remains the most socially accepted form of intimate relationship in Nepal. “Single women may still experience exclusion in a family centred society where conversations and social life often revolve around spouses and children.”

At the same time, she rejects the assumption that unmarried women are necessarily lonely, stating that many build meaningful lives through friendships, work and other forms of social support.

According to Shreya Sanjel, a legal professional at the Supreme Court, Nepal’s laws do not explicitly discriminate against women based on whether they are married or unmarried. Constitutional guarantees of equality prohibit discrimination on the basis of marital status and unmarried women enjoy the same rights to own property, vote, travel and inherit property as married women.

However, Sanjel argues that the gap lies less in the law itself than in the assumptions embedded within legal and administrative systems.

“Legally, there is no clear distinction between married and unmarried individuals. But in practice, you can see differences,”she says.

One example is identity documentation. From citizenship records to banking and voter registration, women are often recognised through their father's or husband's identity, while men are rarely identified through their wives. Although these practices do not deny rights to unmarried women, they reflect an assumption that a woman's identity eventually becomes linked to marriage.

Sanjel also points to legal language that reinforces social attitudes. The Constitution, for instance, refers to "single helpless women", a phrase she believes wrongly equates singlehood with vulnerability. Likewise, some court judgments in rape cases continue to discuss how sexual violence affects a woman's "marriage prospects", framing the harm in relation to marriageability rather than bodily autonomy.

Overall, Sanjel says the barriers faced by women who consciously remain unmarried are less about formal legal restrictions than about social norms that continue to shape the interpretation and implementation of the law.

"The law itself does not restrict women from living independently," she says. "The challenge is that society does not always accept those rights in practice."

articles.title: The case for Indigenous political thought
articles.summary:
“A child of the Earth goes back to the Earth.A child of the Sun goes back to the Sun.A child of the Moon goes back to the Moon.”

This sacred passage from the Mundhum is recited in dialogic form by Tutu-tumyahangs—learned elders and keepers of Indigenous wisdom—during Limbu Indigenous death ceremonies. At first glance, these lines speak of human mortality. Read more closely, however, they express a profound Indigenous political thought: Human existence is inseparable from the Earth and the wider cosmos, and life is sustained through relationships of reciprocity rather than domination. Embedded within this brief passage is a political philosophy that understands nature not as property to be possessed or exploited, but as the source of life to which all beings ultimately return.

As Nepal marks its 31st Indigenous Peoples’ Day, the government, policymakers and those engaged in the country’s development would do well to pay closer attention to the dozens of Indigenous communities whose diverse political traditions and philosophies have long sustained their societies. These Indigenous political thoughts are living intellectual traditions that offer vital insights for reimagining Nepal’s development, deepening its democracy, and building a more just peace as the country confronts profound political and environmental challenges.

It is useful to consider what political thought is, and how Indigenous political thought might help us reimagine our present and future by recognising the diversity of thinking and being.

In The Rights of War and Peace, historian Richard Tuck divides political thought into the ancient and the modern—the former being collectivistic and the latter individualistic. More broadly, he explains that such thought emerges and evolves in response to defining historical and contemporary political, economic and social crises. The emergence of the liberal order in the post-World War II period, its gradual demise, and the rise of China shaping the world order are examples of such dynamics. Another historian, Richard Whatmore, conceives of political thought—whether Western or ‘Oriental’—as full of complexities and paradoxes: sacred, tragic, nationalistic and utopian, shaped by time and space. Today, we witness such complexities: People are wealthier than in the 1900s, yet inequality is stark; societies are more technologically sophisticated, yet these advances have deepened—or will deepen—divisions; and while some countries are better able to withstand escalating climate harms, others face existential threats. At this crossroads, Indigenous political thought offers a space to reimagine the future.

To be sure, Indigenous political thought has not only always existed, but has also profoundly shaped global trade, world politics, economics and science for centuries. The idea of egalitarianism, interdependence and autonomy—some key tenets of liberalism—is said to be drawn from North American Indigenous thought.

In Asia, as James Scott states, most Indigenous communities maintained political autonomy and self-governance guided by their own philosophical traditions, away from modern states, including by resisting colonial subjugation up until the late 19th century. This is certainly the case for various Indigenous communities in Nepal and many other South and Southeast Asian countries that lived under their own governance structures. Like (non-Indigenous) political thought, Indigenous political thought also evolved in response to colonial contexts. At its core, the thought is not a set of abstract political theories centred on modern-state sovereignty and its sanctioned legal order; rather, it is grounded in the right to self-determination, governance based on reciprocity, legal pluralism, collectivity, forgiveness, reconciliation rooted in history, place (land), relationship and spirituality.

To understand Indigenous political thought, one need not be Indigenous. Nor is discussing it an attempt to dismiss or displace non-Indigenous political thought. Rather, it broadens the intellectual terrain of political inquiry and at times helps explore impossibilities. While the former has endured through centuries of colonial violence and continues to evolve, the latter has generated diverse, often competing traditions—some associated with empire, colonialism, fascism, Nazism, communism and capitalism; others with democracy, constitutionalism, human rights and emancipation. Political thought, be it Indigenous or non-Indigenous, has never been singular; it has always emerged from particular histories, places and struggles.

Unfortunately, academic discussion, including policymaking spaces, often approaches political thought through a reductive framework of right and wrong, celebrating some traditions while dismissing others. Such an approach forecloses dialogue and obscures the historical conditions from which political ideas and new policy interventions emerge. The task of engaging Indigenous political thought, therefore, is neither to talk back to the canon nor merely to look back at history. Rather, it is to move the conversation forward while remaining attentive to the legacies of historical violence, dispossession and injustice, as well as to moments of political innovation and transformation.

Addressing climate crises and advancing justice, forgiveness and reconciliation—at least from legal and humanistic perspectives—are grounded in principles long articulated within Indigenous political thought. In 2021, United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres urged humanity to end its “senseless and suicidal war with nature.” Building on this call, the 2024 UN Biodiversity Conference (COP16) called humanity to live “in balance and in harmony with Mother Earth” while recognising the knowledge, innovations and practices of Indigenous Peoples as indispensable to restoring that relationship.

Meeting today’s ecological, social, economic and political crises demands the courage to move beyond familiar theories, policies and practices—to embrace different ways of knowing, deliberate across worldviews, and take seriously the ideas that are too often dismissed. In that sense, Indigenous political thought has much to offer for confronting these crises and reorienting governance. Yet no enduring transformation in governance is possible without first transforming how we understand ourselves, our responsibilities to others, and our place within the living world.

Ultimately, our common future will not be secured by material accumulation, economic growth or technological innovation alone. Nor will our emotional well-being and harmonious relationships with one another and nature depend on wealth. What is needed is the courage to imagine political possibilities that today may seem improbable. That requires asking deeper questions—questions Indigenous political thought has long posed: What separates us more than unites us? How do we wish to be remembered? What principles guide our actions? Where do we position ourselves in relation to other beings? As the Mundhum reminds us in the three sacred lines above: Life comes from the earth, dwells upon it briefly, and ultimately returns to where it began. How we choose to spend that brief time, however, is entirely up to us.

articles.title: AI renders analysis cheap, relationships expensive
articles.summary:
Last year I sat across from the managing partner of a small advisory firm while he named a fear most people in his seat keep to themselves. His partners are in their 70s and 80s. Almost all of the firm’s revenue runs through two individuals’ personal relationships. There is no real mechanism for anyone else to bring in work. He put it plainly: If one of them leaves, does the firm just crumble?

That question stayed with me for a year. Here is where it landed after around 125 conversations with owners and partners at small expert firms, and the advisors who work with them: In a world of AI, relationships matter more, not less. The cheaper the machines make everything else, the more the relationship becomes the thing a client is actually paying for.

Start with what AI is actually eating. The analyst layer. The research, the first-draft deck, the market map, the memo, the grind that junior people used to do and firms used to bill for. That work is getting cheap, fast. So what is a client still willing to pay a premium for?

Judgment, and the relationship that lets you apply it at the right moment. A senior partner at a large firm told me his firm has to move from 20 percent of its revenue coming from partner time to something closer to forty. And the forty, he said, is relationship management, influence, and turning insight into action. The part a machine will not do for you. The machine consumed the input. The human still owns the judgment and the timing.

We usually explain the rainmaker with the word charisma, as if it were a gift you are born with. I do not think that is right. The rainmaker’s real edge is discipline, and it is a discipline almost nobody else can afford to run by hand. Hold a live list of the people who matter. Notice when something changes in their world. Always show up with something worth saying.

Sounds simple. It is brutally manual. Someone who does this at a world-class level, professionally, told me each good touch costs him 15 to 20 minutes of research per person. His own word for it was annoying. And very manual. At another firm, the entire relationship history lives in about fifty spreadsheets, kept by hand, that break the moment a company belongs in two categories at once. The CRM they pay for is, in one partner’s words, no brain, just storage.

Run by hand, this discipline caps at what one head can hold. So the rest of the firm’s pipeline stays hostage to referral luck, and that is not a small thing. When I asked owners where their revenue actually comes from, almost none of them had to think about it. Somewhere between 70 and 90 percent came from referrals and warm relationships.

Going in, I assumed the complaint would get me more leads. It almost never did. Out of 40-odd firms, only a handful named leads as their first problem. What came up instead was quieter and scarier: The whole thing runs through one or two people, and no one has a plan for what happens when they stop.

Now put those two facts together. Analysis is getting cheap. The relationship discipline does not scale. Most people read that and conclude the machines win, and the human touch fades into nostalgia. I think they have it backwards.

When analysis was scarce and expensive, having smart analysts was a genuine moat. The relationship was one edge among several. Now that analysis is cheap, and everyone holds the same tools, the relationship discipline is close to the only thing left that a competitor cannot download.

A principal at one boutique put the contrast plainly: broad, generic outreach produces very few serious conversations, while timely outreach to the right person about something they actually care about performs materially better. Mass outreach is worth less precisely because it is cheap and easy to automate. Well-timed relevance is much harder to replicate.
